correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact pole-plus-positive-moment representation in the 2026 source. Standard complete-elliptic endpoint expansions give the branch density \(\rho(1+u)\sim u/[\pi\log^2(16/u)]\). A self-contained scaling argument with \(u=v/n\) yields \(M_n\sim 1/[\pi n^2\log^2(16n)]\), while the pole term is exponentially negligible. The third-derivative asymptotic then follows from the Abelian theorem for the resulting positive regularly varying coefficients. No finite computation is used to establish an infinite claim.

value.rationale: The 2026 paper resolves an endpoint absolute-monotonicity conjecture by proving signs for an infinite coefficient tail. The accepted result quantifies that tail at the exact borderline regularly varying scale and transfers it to a sharp blow-up law for the distinguished absolutely monotone third derivative. This reveals the analytic strength of the endpoint singularity and gives a natural benchmark for further elliptic-quotient estimates; it is not a routine numerical refinement.
